newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - January 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - January 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Thursday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Dalai Lama to visit Taiwan in late March.
- Dozen of lawmakers and provincial assemblymen suspected of receiving bribes in Chungshan highway construction scandal.
- Professional baseball players detained after admitting to fixing games for illegal profits.
- Twenty-eight people questioned for insurance fraud.
- Bill Clinton expresses dissatisfaction over communist China's human rights record.
- South Korean anti-nuclear activists begin hunger strike in a bid to pressure Taiwan to cancel nuclear waste shipment to North Korea.
- Cabinet faces tough test in major public construction problems.
- Liquidity is loose despite approach of lunar Chinese new year.
- U.S. dollar continues to rise against yen in overseas markets.
- Board directors of listed companies will face punishment if they do not hold enough shares of their companies.
